title: SLO Root-Cause Translation and Remediation Workshop Template
author: Priya Mehta
content:
Summary:
This page provides a reproducible workshop template for translating an SLO failure or concerning error‑budget trend into concrete capacity and remediation actions. Use this template as part of the post‑incident or monthly SLO review cadence to ensure fixes are (a) scoped with measurable acceptance criteria, (b) costed for capacity impact, and (c) assigned clear owners and timelines.

Intent and when to use:
- After any incident where an SLO (latency, availability, quality) was breached or came within 10% of burning the monthly budget.
- During periodic SLO health reviews when an error‑budget trend shows regression for 2+ weeks across key tenants.
- Pre‑deployment reviews for large model/infra changes that risk SLO consumption.

Participants (roles and responsibilities):
1) Incident Facilitator (SRE lead) — runs the workshop, keeps time, enforces scope.
2) Service Owner (feature/product owner) — provides user impact context and acceptance criteria.
3) Runtime/Infra Engineer — explains runtime telemetry, capacity headroom, and constraints.
4) Observability Engineer — provides query examples, dashboards, and instrumentation gaps.
5) Applied ML / Model Owner (when quality/LLM regressions) — explains prompt/quality regressions and eval results.
6) Finance/Cost Engineering (optional) — reviews cost impact for proposed remediations.

Pre-Workshop artifacts to gather (owner and checklist):
- Incident timeline & evidence clip (owner: Incident Lead): timestamped API traces, example tokens, stack traces.
- SLO definition and current burn (owner: Service Owner): metric definition, SLI query, threshold, rolling window.
- Capacity + topology snapshot (owner: Runtime Engineer): pool sizes, GPU types, headroom, recent scale events.
- Sample traffic replay and representative prompt set (owner: Applied ML or QA): 50–500 sample requests prioritized by customer impact.
- Cost delta estimate template pre-filled (owner: Finance/Cost Eng): cost per vGPU/hour, estimated hours for fix, and maintenance overhead.

Workshop agenda (90–120 minutes):
1) 0–10m: Goals & success criteria — facilitator defines what "done" means (e.g., <1% monthly SLO burn within 30 days, or rollback plan + canary for new model).
2) 10–30m: Alignment on facts — short readouts of timeline, SLO metric, capacity snapshot, and sample failing traces.
3) 30–60m: Root‑cause translation exercise — map observed symptoms to probable failure modes using the RCA matrix below.
4) 60–90m: Remediation ideation & selection — generate candidate remediations, cost, risk, and quickness-to-rollout. Prioritize with ICE (Impact, Confidence, Effort) scoring.
5) 90–110m: Action assignment and acceptance criteria — owners, timelines, verification checks, rollback triggers.
6) 110–120m: Publish notes & required follow-ups (doc owners, testing windows, QBR inclusion).

RCA translation matrix (example):
- Symptom: latency p99 spike during morning peak
  - Possible root causes: sudden tail‑latency due to co‑tenant eviction; model cold starts; KV cache thrashing on large context.
  - Evidence to validate: per‑token compute time vs. queuing time; pod restart events; model load times.

- Symptom: sustained error‑budget burn for embeddings endpoint
  - Possible root causes: model degradation after quantization change; traffic shift to heavy embedding clients; upstream payload format changes.
  - Evidence: quality eval diffs; request size distribution; recent rollout tags.

Candidate remediation categories (with examples):
- Configure runtime shims (fastest): e.g., prefer smaller model variant for cheap tenants, enforce max input tokens, apply per‑token admission controls.
- Observability fixes (low cost, high leverage): increase SLI granularity (region, tenant), add synthetic canaries, instrument model variant labels.
- Capacity changes (medium time/cost): add hot replica pool, increase reserved GPU counts for a specific tenant, tune autoscaler thresholds.
- Model changes (higher risk/cost): rollback quantized variant, re‑train prompt anchoring, apply small parameter fine‑tune.
- Traffic shaping (operational & customer coordination): token quotas, rate limits, burst credits with finance approval.

Decision table (use during remediation selection):
- Columns: Candidate, Expected impact (SLO delta), Confidence, Estimated hours to implement, Revert risk, Cost delta/month, Owner.
- Fill example row: Prefer-small-model-by-tenant | -2% SLO burn | 0.8 | 8h to implement | low | +$400/month | Runtime Team

ICE prioritization quick formula (workshop):
- Impact: 0–10 (SLO reduction estimate translated to points)
- Confidence: 0–10 (evidence strength)
- Effort: 0–10 (implementation time in relative points, lower is better)
- ICE score = (Impact * Confidence) / max(1, Effort)

Verification & acceptance criteria templates (copy into ticket):
- Success metric: “After rollout, observed monthly p99 latency reduced to <= X ms or monthly error‑budget burn < Y% over a 30‑day rolling window.”
- Test plan: synthetic replay of 1M tokens with 95th percentile latency target measured; tenant samples in prod shadow for 72 hours.
- Rollback triggers: sustained SLO regression > 25% of pre‑fix within 24h or error rate spike > 2x baseline.

Instrumentation & queries (examples):
- SLI (Prometheus) example for p95 latency on text-generation endpoints:
  - prometheus: rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",le!="+Inf"}[5m])
- Error budget burn rate (pseudo PromQL):
  - increase(api_errors_total{service="generation"}[30d]) / increase(api_requests_total{service="generation"}[30d])
- Hot pool utilization (Kubernetes metrics):
  - avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{pool="hot"}[1h])
- Synthetic canary script example (bash):
  - #!/usr/bin/env bash
    for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
      curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"canary test"}' >/dev/null
    done

Ticket + runbook creation checklist (copy to JIRA ticket):
- Summary: concise problem statement
- Root cause hypothesis: up to 3 bullet points
- Proposed action(s) and ICE score
- Owner + due date
- Verification steps and rollback criteria (copy acceptance template)
- Cost estimate and approval (if > $1,000/month)
- Link to sample failing traces and synthetic replay inputs

Follow-up governance rules:
- Any remediation that changes fleet capacity requires a preapproved maintenance window and cost signoff if monthly delta > $1k.
- Remediations with uncertain impact (Confidence < 0.5) must be canaried for 72 hours before global roll.
- If multiple teams propose conflicting capacity actions, SRE prioritizes by ICE and customer impact; escalate to SRE management if unresolved after 3 business days.

Example outcomes from a workshop (fictional):
- Root cause: quantized model variant increased token decoding tail; evidence: per‑step kernel time increased for last 128 tokens.
- Chosen remediation: revert to previous quantization profile for production traffic and create a canary with 5% traffic to the new quantized profile with 7‑day evaluation (owner: Runtime; due: 2026‑03‑02).
- Verification: synthetic replay with 500k tokens shows p99 latency improvement from 1.9s to 1.2s; reward: accepted.

Templates and artifacts (copyable):
- RCA note template: "Observed, Impact, Hypotheses (1..n), Evidence, Tests to run, Chosen fix, Owner, ETA"
- Action item tracker CSV header: "id,summary,owner,impact,confidence,effort,ice_score,eta,status,verification_link"

Related runbooks/pages to consult in the workshop:
- eng-sre/runbooks/slo-evolution-capacity-simulations-runbook-2025
- eng-sre/capacity-planning/service-capacity-governance-and-error-budget-handbook-2025
- eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/oom-cascade-and-memory-throttling-runbook-2026

Maintenance cadence:
- Save workshop notes into the service's incident folder and add a monthly check to confirm actions progressed.
- SRE Lead will schedule a 30‑day post‑implementation review to evaluate whether the remediation met acceptance criteria.

Appendix: quick PromQL snippets and example dashboard widgets (copy into Grafana)
- Rolling error budget remaining (30d):
  - 1 - (increase(api_errors_total[30d]) / increase(api_requests_total[30d]))
- Per‑tenant p99 latency heatmap query suggestion: use label_replace to collapse tenant tags beyond top N.
